title: Framework Python-maintenance contract permits future token and secret exposure outside its reviewed publisher input
title_de: Framework-Python-Wartungsvertrag erlaubt künftige Token- und Secret-Exposition außerhalb seines überprüften Publisher-Inputs
protocol: GitHub Actions token and secret handling
technical_claim: Before remediation, the new Python-maintenance workflow was exempted as a whole from the generic GitHub-token reference check. Its maintenance-specific helper searched only for literal github.token in resolve and candidate-validate and did not inspect publish. A future YAML change with github['token'], secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN, secrets.<name>, or a publisher shell/action token reference could pass the local security contract even though the intended invariant permits only the explicit create-pull-request.with.token value ${{ github.token }}. The first local repair rejected those direct forms, but its regex still accepted serialized GitHub-expression contexts such as ${{ toJSON(secrets) }} and ${{ toJSON(github) }}. The active narrow follow-up parses expression bodies and rejects secret contexts, GitHub token/index forms, and bare GitHub-context serialization at every non-approved parsed location.
entry_point: A future proposed edit to .github/workflows/check-python-version.yml evaluated by ci/checks/security/check-ci-security-contract.py.
source_to_sink_or_broken_control: Before remediation, the filename allow-list bypassed github_token_reference_errors for the maintenance workflow. The special matcher then recognized only literal github.token and was applied only to resolve/candidate-validate. A secrets.* expression in a read-only job or a sensitive expression in publisher env, run, or another action could therefore reach a job/action/Bash execution context without contract rejection. The repaired SENSITIVE_REFERENCE parser traverses values recursively and permits exactly one parsed publisher field.
attacker_prerequisites: A proposed modification to the Framework maintenance workflow contains an explicit GitHub token or repository/organization secret reference.
That modification is reviewed or merged despite relying on the incomplete local contract; no current untrusted pull-request-to-writer path is established.
observed_behavior: The focused pre-fix regression inserted ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }} into resolve.env and expected rejection. The checker returned no maintenance-contract error, causing the regression to fail. Source review separately established the same parser omission for generic secrets, indexed github['token'], and publisher contexts. After the first repair, a follow-up mutation with ${{ toJSON(secrets) }} in a candidate shell step still returned no error and failed the focused test; a publisher ${{ toJSON(github) }} mutation was likewise accepted. The active expression-aware mutation suite rejects each class while the legitimate workflow passes.
expected_behavior: Resolve and candidate-validate must declare no explicit GitHub token or secret reference, including direct, indexed, shell, or serialized GitHub-expression context forms. Publish may declare exactly one sensitive reference: create-pull-request.with.token must equal ${{ github.token }}. The automatic read-scoped token used internally by actions/checkout is not an explicit YAML secret declaration and remains constrained by contents: read plus persist-credentials: false.
impact: This is a low-severity defense-in-depth control failure: a future workflow edit could introduce a secret into a shell or action without the intended contract rejecting it. The current source has no such extra reference, no pull_request_target trigger, and a schedule/manual trusted-default-branch-gated writer; no current secret disclosure, arbitrary untrusted execution, or broader repository write was reproduced.
preconditions: The maintenance workflow runs under GitHub Actions with the relevant job permissions.
A later source change adds an explicit expression or shell token reference beyond the single reviewed pull-request action input.
reproduction: Copy the parsed current maintenance workflow in tests/ci_security/test_framework_ci_security_contract.py.
Run the focused contract tests before the remediation and observe that python_version_maintenance_errors returns no rejection for that mutation.

evidence.command: RTK-wrapped Framework CI-security-contract unittest using literal inert ${{ toJSON(secrets) }} and ${{ toJSON(github) }} test expressions
evidence.summary: The pre-follow-up mutation failed because the direct-reference matcher accepted serialized contexts. The same retained evidence records the post-fix focused 12-test pass; no credential was resolved, printed, or retained.

evidence.summary: The complete follow-up security-diff scan sealed with zero reportable findings and records the serialized-context bypass as safely reproduced and closed by the current expression-aware contract.

root_cause: A file-wide allow-list was used where a parsed, location-specific exception was required. The special matcher checked only github.token, omitted indexed github['token'], secrets.* and shell GITHUB_TOKEN forms, and did not validate the publisher outside its create-pull-request token option. The first repair still used a direct-reference regex and therefore did not classify a bare secrets or github context nested inside a GitHub expression function.
proposed_remediation: Active follow-up: retain generic compatibility handling for unrelated workflows, but parse GitHub expression bodies before recursively classifying maintenance-workflow values. Reject secrets anywhere in an expression, github.token, every github[...] form, bare github serialization, and shell GITHUB_TOKEN in resolve/candidate-validate and every publish location except the unique reviewed create-pull-request.with.token field, which must equal ${{ github.token }}. Mutation regressions preserve github.sha, github.repository, and the legitimate current publisher token input.
acceptance_criteria: A resolve or candidate-validate env, with, uses, or run expression using github.token, github['token'], secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN, another secrets.* form, or serialized secrets/github context is rejected.
A publisher shell, env, or non-approved action reference, including serialized github context, is rejected.
The only accepted sensitive publisher expression is the unique create-pull-request.with.token scalar ${{ github.token }}.
The current workflow and focused/full Framework contract checks pass without adding permissions, triggers, secret sources, or auto-merge behavior.
validation_plan: Rerun the focused mutation test after the checker change and verify all injected classes are rejected while the current workflow passes.
Review the changed expression-aware traversal for alternate direct, indexed, serialized, and shell token/secret spellings and the publisher action count/location.
Run the owning Framework contract suite, full lint, documentation/Change-Record validation, git diff --check, and final security-diff scan before delivery; then collect exact-head hosted PR evidence.
legitimate_control_tests: The actual check-python-version.yml permits its one explicit peter-evans/create-pull-request.with.token: ${{ github.token }} input.
Read-only checkout continues to use its implicit read-scoped GitHub Actions credential without a persisted checkout credential or an explicit YAML token/secret reference.
bypass_review: Test github.token, github['token'], dynamic github indexing, secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN, generic secrets.<name>, bracket-form secrets references, serialized toJSON(secrets), serialized toJSON(github), and shell ${GITHUB_TOKEN} in both reader jobs and all publisher fields. Confirm that only the exact parsed token field is excluded, that github.sha and github.repository remain benign, that a duplicate create-pull-request action cannot create another exception, and that checkout's implicit default token is described accurately rather than mistaken for an explicit secret declaration.
deduplication_note: No existing Framework finding owns this new, uncommitted CPython-maintenance workflow token/secret contract. The issue is distinct from broader GitHub governance and historical workflow-permission records because it is an independently remediable parsed semantic control.
evidence_limitations: The regression uses literal non-secret test expressions only; no credential was created, printed, or retained.
The observation proves a static safety-contract bypass that would require a future source change and merge; it does not prove a current secret disclosure or untrusted pull-request execution path.
GitHub automatic per-job token behavior is hosted-runtime behavior; this record constrains explicit YAML exposure and preserves the read-only checkout configuration.
residual_risk: The expression-aware repair and complete local gates are validated, but the remediated commit has not yet been pushed and exact-current-head GitHub Actions, review, and SonarQube evidence remain pending. Current workflow source remains schedule/manual only, default-branch/repository gated for publication, Draft-only, and without the unsafe expressions used in the reproduction.

history.detail: A focused task-owned mutation regression demonstrated that secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN in resolve.env was accepted by the maintenance contract. The finding was allocated as a P2/low Framework hardening remediation before product delivery.

The parser now recursively rejects explicit token/secret references outside the unique reviewed publisher token field, including github['token']. Focused mutation regressions, Python-version and CI-security contracts, full Framework lint, git diff --check, and the sealed complete security-diff scan passed. Exact-head Draft-PR evidence remains pending.

A safe literal mutation demonstrated that the prior direct-reference regex still accepted ${{ toJSON(secrets) }} and ${{ toJSON(github) }}. The finding is reopened for an expression-aware parser/test repair; no current secret disclosure or untrusted PR-to-writer path was observed.

The expression-aware matcher rejects serialized secrets/github contexts, dynamic GitHub indexing, direct token/secret forms, and shell GITHUB_TOKEN outside the one approved publisher input while preserving github.sha and github.repository. The safe pre/post regression, 36 focused tests, 85 CI-security tests, native workflow/documentation/lint gates, and the sealed follow-up security-diff scan passed. Exact current-head hosted delivery validation remains required before any verified disposition.
